title.value: Aligning artificial intelligence with climate change mitigation
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Aligning artificial intelligence with climate change mitigation

extractions.description: This paper introduces a systematic framework for describing Machine Learning (ML)'s effects on Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, comprising three categories: (A) compute-related impacts, (B) immediate impacts of applying ML, and (C) system-level impacts. It assesses and prioritizes research and data needs for impact assessment and scenario analysis, and identify important policy levers.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on aligning AI with climate change mitigation, making sustainable development a central theme.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: To explicitly and consistently account for ML in long-term climate and energy projections, and in the design of appropriate policies, the research community needs to develop a holistic and operational understanding of the different ways in which ML can positively and negatively impact climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies

primary_category.justification: The paper's primary focus is on how AI and ML can be used to mitigate climate change.
primary_category.quote: Aligning artificial intelligence with climate change mitigation

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper provides a general framework for assessing the impact of AI on climate change mitigation, without focusing on a specific sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: We therefore introduce a systematic framework for describing ML’s effects on GHG emissions, comprising three categories: (A) compute-related impacts, (B) immediate impacts of applying ML, and (C) system-level impacts

applications.value: Policy design, monitoring, and enforcement (e.g. GHG tracking, infrastructure maps)
applications.justification: ML can be used to translate raw data such as text documents or satellite imagery into usable insights for RD&D, policy-making, and systems planning – e.g., by tracking GHG emissions, fusing datasets, or gathering information on building efficiency characteristics.
applications.quote: For example, via data mining and remote sensing, ML can be used to translate raw data such as text documents or satellite imagery into usable insights for RD&D, policy-making, and systems planning – e.g., by tracking GHG emissions, fusing datasets, or gathering information on building efficiency characteristics.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper falls within the existing categories.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new sub-category.
